Geospatial Logistics Data: UN/LOCODE, Geofencing & PostGIS

13 min read Updated: November 2026 By Rajvardhan Singh Rathore
Physical logistics is fundamentally geospatial. Learn how to normalize global port and terminal codes (UN/LOCODE, IATA) and execute real-time geofence polygon checks using PostGIS spatial indexes.

UN/LOCODE, IATA & SPLC Standards

Global logistics data integrates three major location code taxonomies:

  • UN/LOCODE (United Nations Code for Trade and Transport Locations): 5-character string consisting of 2-letter ISO country code + 3-character location identifier (e.g., USLAX = Los Angeles Port, SGSIN = Singapore, NLRTM = Rotterdam).
  • IATA / ICAO: 3-letter airport codes used for air cargo logistics (e.g., MEM, FRA, HKG).
  • SPLC (Standard Point Location Code): 6-9 digit numeric code used in North American rail and motor freight.

PostGIS Spatial DDL & Polygon Modeling

PostGIS Spatial DDL 
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS postgis;

CREATE TABLE logistics_geofenced_hubs (
  hub_id UUID PRIMARY KEY,
  unlocode CHAR(5) NOT NULL,
  hub_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  facility_type VARCHAR(30) CHECK (facility_type IN ('PORT', 'AIRPORT', 'RAIL_RAMP', 'CROSS_DOCK', 'LAST_MILE_DEPOT')),
  geofence_polygon GEOMETRY(Polygon, 4326) NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

CREATE INDEX idx_hubs_spatial ON logistics_geofenced_hubs USING GIST (geofence_polygon);

Automated Geofence Entry/Exit Detection

When a container telematics unit broadcasts GPS coordinates, determine if the asset has arrived within the terminal geofence using ST_Contains:

PostGIS Point-in-Polygon Query 
SELECT 
  p.container_id,
  p.ping_timestamp,
  h.unlocode,
  h.hub_name,
  h.facility_type
FROM container_gps_pings p
JOIN logistics_geofenced_hubs h 
  ON ST_Contains(
       h.geofence_polygon, 
       ST_SetSRID(ST_MakePoint(p.longitude, p.latitude), 4326)
     )
WHERE p.ping_timestamp >= CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '15 minutes';

R-Tree Spatial Indexing & Performance

Always maintain a GiST spatial index on polygon and point columns. For distance queries across broad geographic areas, use the GEOGRAPHY type to automatically account for the Earth's ellipsoidal curvature.
